clue.text: Greek character taking possession of a Hebridean island, backward place

indicators.note: backward tells us to read the whole run of pieces from right to left
taking possession of means the Greek letter is followed by, and so holds, the island and the article

parts.note: eta is the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet
Coll is an island in the Inner Hebrides, off western Scotland

explanation.surface: A Greek seizes a Scottish island and somewhere remote.
explanation.walkthrough: The Greek letter 'taking possession of' the island and A is all one string; 'backward' turns the whole of it, so ETA ends up at the end as ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To place things is to assign or distribute them to positions, a synonym in the sense of allotting.

clue.text: Expects carol-singers by afternoon

indicators.note: by means set beside the other piece

parts.note: A abbreviates afternoon here
waits are, in Britain, groups of carol-singers going door to door at Christmas

explanation.surface: Someone expects carol-singers by the afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waits' is an old British word for street carol-singers.
explanation.definitionFit: To anticipate something is to look forward to it or wait for it.

clue.text: Flexible part of field gun

definitions.meaning: the two-wheeled front carriage to which a gun's trail is hitched for towing

explanation.definitionFit: Supple describes the adjective; the noun is the detachable fore-part of a gun carriage.

clue.text: False report about a new plastic

indicators.note: about means going round the other pieces

parts.note: plastic is slang for a credit card

explanation.surface: Untrue rumours spread about a new credit card.
explanation.walkthrough: CARD goes 'about' A and N; 'plastic' is a card.
explanation.definitionFit: A baseless rumour or hoax story, from the French for duck.

clue.text: Market in centre of new estate is marked out in squares

definitions.note: a participle phrase standing for the verb, to mark out in squares

indicators.note: in centre of means placed in the middle of the other piece
new means the letters of 'estate' are made anew, rearranged

parts.note: to market goods is to sell them

explanation.surface: A shop at the heart of a housing estate is laid out in a grid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' looks like an adjective describing the estate, but it is the anagram signal; 'is' is a link, so the definition is the verb phrase 'marked out in squares'.
explanation.definitionFit: To tile a surface with shapes fitting together without gaps, like a chessboard.

clue.text: Simple life, confined to a cell?

definitions.text: Simple life, confined to a cell?

parts.words: Simple life, confined to a cell?
parts.note: reads like a prisoner's austere existence, but describes a single-celled organism, a very simple form of life

explanation.surface: A monk or prisoner living plainly in a cell.
explanation.definitionFit: This organism is a primitive single-celled creature, a lifeform whose whole body is one cell.

clue.text: Nice people, some of them?

parts.note: Nice is the French city, not the adjective; some of its people are ladies, addressed in the French plural

explanation.surface: A remark that only some folk are pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: French plural form of address for married women, ladies in the city of Nice.

clue.text: Inadequate notice to cover the French poll

indicators.note: to cover means to wrap round the other piece
inadequate means the word notice is not right as it stands, so rearranged

parts.note: le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: Short notice is given for a vote in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inadequate' is an unusual anagram signal: the notice is not good enough as it is, so its letters are rearranged to ECTION, which then wraps the French article after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A vote to choose representatives, a synonym for a ballot.

clue.text: Give up one's seat to the next person in line?

definitions.text: Give up one's seat to the next person in line?

parts.words: Give up one's seat to the next person in line?
parts.note: sounds like polite bus etiquette, but describes a monarch renouncing the throne to the heir

explanation.surface: Offering your seat to the next person in a queue.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruler renouncing the throne, passing the crown to the heir in the line of succession.

clue.text: A receiving apparatus Scotsman's installed to give warning

indicators.note: the Scotsman is installed, fitted inside the receiving apparatus

parts.note: a satellite dish receives broadcast signals
mon is a Scots form of 'man'; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: Fitting a satellite dish, a Scot issues a caution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotsman's' is 'Scotsman is', and MON is the Scots word crosswords use for a man; it goes inside the dish after the opening A.
explanation.definitionFit: To reprimand or caution someone is to warn them, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Advantage keeping most of landscape to scale

indicators.note: keeping means holding the other piece inside it

parts.note: in tennis, 'ad' is short for advantage

indicators.note: most of means drop the final letter of the word

parts.note: a landscape is a scene

explanation.surface: Drawing a landscape to scale gives an advantage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advantage' is the tennis score call 'ad', not an edge; 'scale' is the verb to climb, not the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To scale a cliff is to climb it, going upwards.

clue.text: Conservatives accepting ambassador's ideas

indicators.note: accepting means taking the other piece inside

parts.note: Tories are members of the UK Conservative Party
an ambassador is addressed as His Excellency, abbreviated HE

explanation.surface: Tory politicians take up a diplomat's proposals.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypotheses or notions put forward to explain something are synonyms for ideas.

clue.text: Waterproofing agent — it's about to be used in raincoat

indicators.note: used in means placed inside the other word

parts.note: mac, short for mackintosh, is a British word for a raincoat

indicators.note: about means turned round, read backwards

explanation.surface: Something to waterproof a raincoat with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the clue's 'it's' round to STI; 'used in' then puts that inside the British raincoat.
explanation.definitionFit: A resin or putty used as a sealant and waterproof filler.

clue.text: A shortened telescope adapted to catch last of moon's shimmering?

indicators.note: to catch means to take the other letter inside
adapted means the letters are altered into a new order
shortened means the word loses its final letter
last of picks the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Looking through an altered telescope at the moon's glow.
explanation.walkthrough: TELESCOPE 'shortened' is TELESCOP; with A, 'adapted' gives OPALESCET, which 'catches' N.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing a milky iridescence like an opal, shifting colours like light on water.

clue.text: Applauded off, utterly exhausted

parts.note: to applaud is to clap
a light that is off is out

explanation.surface: A performer clapped off stage, worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for worn out, of a person or a decrepit machine.

clue.text: A little hesitation about study featured in theologian's supplement

indicators.note: about means going round the other pieces

parts.note: um is a short hesitant sound

indicators.note: featured in means set inside the other piece

parts.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree
a den is a private room for study

explanation.surface: A theologian hesitates to add an appendix to his study.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers: 'featured in' puts the study inside the theologian's letters, and A plus the hesitation go 'about' that result.
explanation.definitionFit: An addition at the end of a book or document, an appendix.

clue.text: Metal key fitted under barrel on gun

indicators.note: fitted under means placed below the barrel in this down light

parts.note: a tun is a large cask
G is a musical key
the Sten is a British submachine gun

explanation.surface: A metal key fitted under a gun barrel.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down light, 'fitted under barrel' sets the key below, so after, the barrel; 'on' then puts the gun below that.
explanation.definitionFit: A dense chemical element, also called wolfram, used in lamp filaments.

clue.text: In the Navy, gin cocktail's rapidly disappearing

parts.note: a navy is a fleet of ships

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters of 'gin' are mixed

explanation.surface: Sailors' gin cocktails vanish quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasting only a short while, passing quickly, as a brief glimpse.

clue.text: Bet address contains ambiguities

definitions.note: plural noun standing for a mass noun meaning ambiguous speech

parts.note: a double is a bet on two races, winnings rolled from one to the next
an address is a talk or speech

explanation.surface: A gambler's speech is full of ambiguous statements.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberately evasive or equivocal speech is full of things that can be read two ways.

clue.text: Stay composed, and take the wind out of people's sails?

definitions.meaning: read as two words, an instruction to keep calm

definitions.text: take the wind out of people's sails?
definitions.meaning: literally, to leave a sailing ship motionless for lack of wind

explanation.definitionFit: Split, the word is an instruction to keep cool; whole, it means to stall a sailing ship windless.

clue.text: Ordinary seaman breaking old connection, being redundant

indicators.note: breaking means splitting the other pieces open to go inside

parts.note: a tie is a connection or bond

explanation.surface: A sailor breaks an old bond, being surplus to needs.
explanation.walkthrough: OS breaks into OTIE after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Serving no purpose, superfluous or futile.

clue.text: States ballet, oddly, to be of practical value?

parts.note: the States are the USA

indicators.note: oddly picks the odd-numbered letters of ballet

explanation.surface: America finds its ballet a little odd and useful.
explanation.definitionFit: Fit for use, serviceable and functional.

clue.text: Young bird, swallow nursing broken leg

indicators.note: nursing means holding the other piece inside

parts.note: to swallow is to eat

indicators.note: broken means the letters of 'leg' are rearranged

explanation.surface: A swallow chick caring for its broken leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallow' is the verb to eat, not the bird, though the young bird is the definition; 'broken' rearranges LEG to AGL inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A young bird of prey, the offspring of a large raptor.

clue.text: Boasts extravagantly about introduction of extra strong fire retardant

indicators.note: about means going round the other piece
extravagantly means the letters are reworked wildly
introduction of picks the opening letter of each word

explanation.surface: Someone boasts wildly about a strong fireproofing material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extravagantly' rearranges BOASTS to ASBTOS, which goes 'about' ES, the first letters of 'extra strong'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fibrous mineral used to fireproof buildings, a classic heat-resistant material.

clue.text: Small group from Egypt welcomed into Irish parliament

indicators.note: welcomed into means taken inside the other piece

parts.note: the Dail is the lower house of the Irish parliament
ET is the international vehicle registration code for Egypt

explanation.surface: An Egyptian delegation is received in Dublin's parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A military term for a small party of soldiers assigned to a task.

clue.text: Sacrifice both came to misinterpret

indicators.note: misinterpret means the letters are read wrongly, rearranged

explanation.surface: Two people misread the call for a sacrifice.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece, a great public offering of a hundred oxen; now any large-scale slaughter.

clue.text: To control staff takes time

parts.note: to staff a desk is to man it
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Controlling staff takes time.
explanation.definitionFit: To run or be in charge of something is to control it.

clue.text: Rush to see male record overturned in sports arena

indicators.note: in means placed inside the sports arena

parts.note: a stade is an old word for a stadium, the Greek running track

indicators.note: overturned means the record is turned over, read backwards in a down light

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Fans rush to watch a man break a record at the stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' suits a down light but here simply turns the record round to PE; STADE is an old word for a stadium, rarely seen outside crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden mass rush of animals or people in panic.
